source.text: ወዳግመ፡ ጠየቁ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ሐጋይ፡ ከመ፡ ኮነ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ላዕሌሃ፡ በቅድሜሃ፡ ወአንትሙሰ፡ ተኀሥሡ፡ ምጽላለ፡ ወጽላሎተ፡ በእንተ፡ ዋዕየ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወምድርሰ፡ ትውዒ፡ እምቀ፡ ሐሩር፡ ወአንትሙሰ፡ ኢትክሉ፡ ከይዶታ፡ ለምድር፡ ወኢ፡ ኰኵሐ፡ በእንተ፡ ዋዕያ።
source.note: Fresh bounded collation from actual Charles1906 printed6 and8/PDF44 and46. PDF45 is the intervening Greek-facing page, not the Ge’ez continuation. The selected Ge’ez unit is transcribed directly, apparatus numerals omitted and punctuation normalized; the line-break-separated enclitic inወአንትሙሰ is joined. No Betamaṣāḥǝft/oracle text or later English translation supplies this candidate. The earlier canonical oracle-derived text is not treated as proof.

translation.text: Again, observe the days of summer, how the sun is over it at its beginning.[a] You seek shelter and shade[b] because of the heat of the sun, and the earth grows hot with burning heat.[c] You cannot walk upon the earth or a rock because of its heat.

footnotes.text: The selected Ge’ez has a compressed feminine-pronoun expression, literally “over it, before it/at its beginning.” The exact relation to summer is difficult; this rendering does not resolve it into an unstated claim about the sun’s strength.
The Ge’ez uses two related shelter/shade terms; both are retained rather than collapsed into one.

The heat expression crosses the Ge’ez page boundary from printed6 to8. Charles’s printed6 note42 records differing forms. This source record preserves the selected printed formእምቀ followed byሐሩር, rather than supplying a longer normalized word from a digital oracle.
